title: Il present perfect continuous
rule: Have / has + been + verbo in -ing. Per qualcosa che è cominciato nel passato e continua adesso, con l'accento sul processo o sulla durata: I've been working here for six months. Per lo sforzo in corso: I've been trying to call. Per il recente visibile adesso: your hair is wet, I've been swimming. Non si usa con i verbi di stato (know, want, like, need, have = possedere, believe, understand, mean): lì il perfect simple. Negativo haven't / hasn't been + -ing; domanda con inversione. Per / since come al perfect simple. Risposte brevi Yes, I have / No, I haven't (non Yes, I've).

blocks.caption: [[work|lavorare]] · present perfect continuous: affermativo, negativo, domanda

head: Uso
Inglese
Italiano
rows: durata (processo che continua)
I've been working here for six months. We've been living in Bloordale since October.
Lavoro qui da sei mesi. Viviamo a Bloordale da ottobre.
sforzo in corso
I've been trying to call you. We've been looking everywhere.
Ti sto cercando di chiamare da un po'. Stiamo cercando dappertutto.
recente visibile ora
Your eyes are red. — I've been crying. The road is wet: it's been raining.
Hai gli occhi rossi. — Ho pianto. La strada è bagnata: ha piovuto.
domanda su un periodo recente
What have you been doing? Have you been working today?
Cosa hai fatto (ultimamente)? Hai lavorato oggi?
negativo
I haven't been sleeping. He hasn't been eating.
Non sto dormendo. Non sta mangiando.

blocks.caption: Verbi di stato: solo simple
head: Da non usare al continuous
Giusto
rows: I've been knowing her for a year.
I've known her for a year.
I've been having this phone.
I've had this phone for two years.
I've been liking it.
I've liked it since the first day.
I've been understanding.
I've understood.
blocks.note: Know, have (own), want, like, love, need, prefer, mean, believe, understand, seem, hate: perfect simple.

blocks.title: Vivo da sei mesi / I've been living
blocks.text: L'italiano usa il presente + da: [[vivo qui da sei mesi]]. L'inglese ha due scelte: [[I've lived here for six months]] (perfect simple, neutro) o [[I've been living here for six months]] (perfect continuous, con un po' più di enfasi sulla durata). Per un lavoro: [[I've been working]] enfatizza che continua; [[I've worked]] è più neutro. Entrambi corretti, entrambi usati.

items.t: I've been baking since four. I've baked thirty croissants.
items.n: Sto facendo il pane dalle quattro. Ho sfornato trenta croissant.

items.t: Have you been running? — No, I've been walking fast. I'm late.
items.n: Hai corso? — No, ho camminato veloce. Sono in ritardo.

items.t: She's been thinking about moving back since Christmas. She hasn't decided.
items.n: Pensa di tornare da Natale. Non ha deciso.

items.t: I've known Chiara for a year, but I've been working with her for six months.
items.n: Conosco Chiara da un anno, ma lavoro con lei da sei mesi.

items.wrong: I'm working here since October. I work here for six months.
items.right: I've been working here since October. I've worked here for six months.

items.wrong: I've been knowing her. I've been having this phone.
items.right: I've known her. I've had this phone.

items.wrong: I've been working since six months.
items.right: I've been working for six months. / I've been working since October.

items.wrong: Have been you crying? I been crying.
items.right: Have you been crying? I've been crying.

items.q: Chiara ___ (be, work) at the bakery ___ October. She ___ (be, live) in Bloordale ___ six months.
items.n: Chiara lavora alla panetteria da ottobre. Vive a Bloordale da sei mesi.

items.q: What have you been doing? — I've been messaging you for a week.
answers: What have you been doing? I've been messaging you for a week
